concepts.title: The Indian National Congress and the National Movement

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Indian National Congress and the National Movement' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian National Congress, founded in Bombay in 1885, became the main platform of the freedom struggle, moving from early moderate petitions to mass agitation as leaders and people joined hands against colonial rule.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Indian National Congress and the National Movement'.
questions.a: From petition to protest: the Congress turned elite demands into a people's movement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Indian National Congress and the National Movement' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: hees202.txt lines 58-100 (Indian National Congress in Bombay), 452-520 (rise of the national movement))

concepts.title: Purna Swaraj and the Mass Movements

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Purna Swaraj and the Mass Movements' refers to.
questions.a: The demand crystallised as Purna Swaraj - complete independence - proclaimed in 1929-30; Gandhian movements of non-cooperation and civil disobedience, salt marches and boycotts drew millions into open defiance of British rule.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Purna Swaraj and the Mass Movements'.
questions.a: Purna Swaraj turned the goal from dominion status to complete independence, fought with non-violent mass action.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Purna Swaraj and the Mass Movements' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Revolutionaries, Azad Hind and the Armed Challenge

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Revolutionaries, Azad Hind and the Armed Challenge' refers to.
questions.a: Alongside non-violence ran the armed stream - revolutionaries who fought and sacrificed - and Subhas Chandra Bose's Azad Hind movement, which proclaimed a provisional government and led the Indian National Army against the British during the Second World War.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Revolutionaries, Azad Hind and the Armed Challenge'.
questions.a: From underground revolutionaries to the Azad Hind Fauj, armed resistance complemented the mass movement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Revolutionaries, Azad Hind and the Armed Challenge' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: hees202.txt lines 149-220 (navy mutiny, Azad Hind proclaimed, royal proclamation))

concepts.title: Social Reform and the Awakening: Roy, Bankim and Syed Ahmad Khan

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Social Reform and the Awakening: Roy, Bankim and Syed Ahmad Khan' refers to.
questions.a: The nineteenth-century awakening ran through reformers - Raja Ram Mohan Roy against sati and for modern education, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay whose Vande Mataram stirred patriotism from the 1860s-70s, and Syed Ahmad Khan promoting education among Muslims - alongside movements like the Arya Samaj.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Social Reform and the Awakening: Roy, Bankim and Syed Ahmad Khan'.
questions.a: Reformers fought social evils and spread education, preparing the soil of nationalism.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Social Reform and the Awakening: Roy, Bankim and Syed Ahmad Khan' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: hees202.txt lines 301-350 (Bankim Chandra, Syed Ahmad Khan, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Arya Samaj))
